title: Describing data and trends
description: Academic Task 1 language: verbs, nouns, adjectives and adverbs for describing changes, proportions and comparisons in charts and tables.

words.definition: to fall very quickly and suddenly by a large amount
words.example: Sales of DVDs plummeted after streaming services became popular.

words.definition: to rise and fall repeatedly
words.example: The price of rice fluctuated between $400 and $500 per tonne over the decade.

words.definition: to increase suddenly and strongly
words.example: Demand for electric bikes surged in 2021.

words.definition: to reach the highest point
words.example: Visitor numbers peaked at 1.2 million in August before falling sharply.

words.definition: to stop rising or falling and stay at the same level
words.example: After rising for five years, unemployment levelled off at around 6%.

words.definition: to stay at the same level after a period of change
words.example: Internet use among teenagers has plateaued at close to 100%.

words.definition: a gradual decrease in amount or quality
words.example: There was a steady decline in the number of smokers between 2000 and 2020.

words.definition: at a regular and even rate
words.example: The population of the city grew steadily throughout the period.

words.definition: by a very small amount
words.example: The figure for women was marginally higher than that for men.

words.definition: suddenly and to a very large degree
words.example: Car ownership rose dramatically in the 1990s.

words.definition: a part of a total, often given as a percentage
words.example: The proportion of students studying abroad doubled over the period.

words.definition: to form a particular amount or part of something
words.example: Rice accounted for just over half of all crops grown in the region.

words.definition: in the same order as the things already mentioned
words.example: Spending on food and housing stood at 30% and 25% respectively.

words.definition: to become greater in number or amount than something else
words.example: By 2015, online sales had overtaken high-street sales.
collocations: overtake X as the most popular

words.definition: the lowest point in a series of figures
words.example: Sales reached a trough in February before recovering in spring.

words.definition: to be at a particular level or amount
words.example: In 2010, the unemployment rate stood at 8%.

words.definition: to be greater than a number or amount
words.example: In both years, exports exceeded imports by a significant margin.

words.definition: happening slowly over a long period
words.example: There was a gradual increase in the average age of first-time buyers.

words.definition: so small that it is not important
words.example: The change in the number of tram users was negligible.

words.definition: approximately, not exactly
words.example: Roughly a third of respondents said they cycled to work.

words.definition: to become twice as large
words.example: The number of international visitors doubled between 2005 and 2015.

words.definition: to reduce by fifty percent
words.example: The cost of solar panels has halved in less than ten years.

words.definition: to increase again after a fall
words.example: Tourist numbers rebounded strongly after travel restrictions were lifted.

words.definition: a general movement towards lower figures
words.example: Newspaper sales show a clear downward trend over the period.

words.definition: a general movement towards higher figures
words.example: Spending on healthcare followed an upward trend throughout the decade.

words.definition: similar in size or amount, so that they can be compared
words.example: The two cities had comparable levels of car ownership in 2020.

words.definition: more than half of a group
words.example: The vast majority of households owned at least one mobile phone.

words.definition: less than half of a group
words.example: Only a small minority of commuters travelled by bicycle.

words.definition: expected or estimated for the future
words.example: The projected figure for 2040 is almost three times the current level.

words.definition: always in the same way or at the same level
words.example: Coal remained consistently the largest source of electricity throughout the period.
